answer: Each fleece is combed until the staple runs long and even, and the comber measures every staple in the book kept per fleece. A raven fleece bought at the wool fair fails the book: at the ember of the staple the fibres must match the comber's own long draw, and fair wool is short and tangled. Forging the book means combing wool for a full season, buying 200 fleeces and paying 10,400 in wool and wages, and the lantern entry in the staple book is read at every cloth hall, so a fleece whose staple was never measured is sent back.
